detail.3: Each tool has a card with a return day and the shelf number.
detail.5: The card is the loan record: return day plus shelf number, kept on the shelf itself.

detail.1: Volunteers look at the shelf twice a week.
detail.3: Twice a week, volunteers set aside anything that needs a repair.
detail.5: A twice-weekly inspection quarantines tools whose condition needs repair.

detail.3: A neighbour borrows a drill, a ladder, or hand tools and brings them back.

text.1: A neighbour takes a tool home for the weekend.
text.3: The loan starts at the shelf and ends when the tool comes back.
text.5: Custody moves from the numbered shelf to the borrower for one weekend.

subtitle.3: The idea stays local, with no fees and a paper log.
subtitle.5: Constraints are locality, zero fees, no delivery route, and a paper borrowing log.

body.1: People borrow a drill, a ladder, or hand tools. They bring them back.
body.3: The shelf stands in the community hall. A paper log records who borrowed what.
body.5: The operating picture is a hall shelf, weekend loans, and a paper log instead of a delivery service.

why.1: A paper log is enough for a small shelf.
why.3: The idea chooses a paper log because there are no fees and no delivery route.
why.5: A paper log matches the no-fee, no-delivery constraint and avoids a separate account system.

why.1: Tools stay at the hall. Nobody delivers them.
why.3: Delivery was set aside so neighbours come to the hall themselves.
why.5: A delivery route was rejected to keep the shelf local and the operating cost at zero.

text.1: The note says a weekend, not an exact hour.
text.3: Return timing is still open beyond the card's return day.
text.5: The return-day field exists, but the grace period after that day is undefined.

q.1: Does the shelf charge a fee?

glossary.definition: The hall place where shared tools wait to be borrowed.
